Rows that cross index block boundaries can cause wrong reverse read results
After migrating data from 2.2.19 to 3.0.30, I noticed that some reverse read could return incorrect results. It happens when a row crosses the index boundary.
h1. Reproduce

Start up cassandra-2.2.19 (single node), set column_index_size_kb to 1. (Using default config should still reproduce it, but it would need a much longer row).

Execute the following commands
{code:java}
CREATE KEYSPACE IF NOT EXISTS ks WITH REPLICATION = { 'class' : 'SimpleStrategy', 'replication_factor' : 1 };
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ks.tb (c0 INT,c1 INT,c3 set<TEXT>,c5 INT,c4 set<TEXT>, PRIMARY KEY (c5, c0 ));
INSERT INTO ks.tb (c4, c3, c5, c0) VALUES ({'v1','v2','v3','','v0'},{'v4','','','v3'},1,2);
INSERT INTO ks.tb (c4, c5, c0) VALUES ({'','VAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA','','','','','v4','','mAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA'},1,411710283);
ALTER TABLE ks.tb DROP c3 ;
ALTER TABLE ks.tb DROP c4 ; {code}
Perform a read in the old version: results are correct
{code:java}
Connected to Test Cluster at 127.0.0.1:9042.
[cqlsh 5.0.1 | Cassandra 2.2.19 | CQL spec 3.3.1 | Native protocol v4]
Use HELP for help.
cqlsh> SELECT *  FROM ks.tb WHERE c5 = 1 ORDER BY c0 DESC
 c5 | c0        | c1
----+-----------+------
  1 | 411710283 | null
  1 |         2 | null

(2 rows) {code}
Drain and upgrade to 3.0.30
{code:java}
bin/nodetool -h ::FFFF:127.0.0.1 drain;bin/nodetool -h ::FFFF:127.0.0.1 stopdaemon; {code}
Perform a read in the new version: it returns 3 rows while there are only 2 rows in the table. (incorrect results)
{code:java}
apache-cassandra-3.0.30 $ bin/cqlsh
Connected to Test Cluster at 127.0.0.1:9042.
[cqlsh 5.0.1 | Cassandra 3.0.30 | CQL spec 3.4.0 | Native protocol v4]
Use HELP for help.
cqlsh> SELECT *  FROM ks.tb WHERE c5 = 1 ORDER BY c0 DESC;
 c5 | c0        | c1
----+-----------+------
  1 | 411710283 | null
  1 | 411710283 | null
  1 |         2 | null

(3 rows) {code}
